Subject: Follow-up: function surface + failover options (post-demo recap)

Hi Sofia / Alex —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can lock the next steps into the PoC plan:

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: multi-step customer support automation (classify intent -> enrich with account data -> call billing tool -> generate structured response).
- Volume profile: 450k calls/month, 95th pct burst ~120rps for short sessions (avg 120 tokens).
- SLA target: p95 end-to-end <350ms for core path; spike tolerance acceptable with graceful degradation.
- Data constraints: account PII but tokenized; will bring SOC2 / legal to finalize retention.

Key architecture/qualification topics we promised to outline
1) Function (tool) surface: which functions to define server-side vs client-invoked, structured output schema for each function.
2) Parallelism and failover: whether to fan-out tools in parallel (call multiple downstreams) vs serial orchestration and how to handle partial failures.
3) Auth + SDK setup: recommended SDKs, auth patterns for hosted vs private, specific headers and token rotation cadence.
4) Embeddings + reranker: hybrid approach for relevance then lightweight rerank to keep latency tight.

Immediate asks from your side
- Confirm the list of downstream tools we will need uncovered (billing API, account enrichment, CRM lookup).
- Share a sample account object (PII redacted) and a short prompt example you expect to run (one or two examples).

Attached: redwood-fn-surface-v1.pdf (draft function definitions + schema), sample PoC timeline.

Proposed next steps
- We (Redwood) to share a concise technical plan for function surface + failover by EOD today.
- Scheduling: 1-hour tech deep-dive next Tue to walk through SDK snippet and auth demos.
- Procurement follow-up: Alex, loop your procurement contact so we can get an MSA review timeline.

Thanks —

Thanks Hannah — that capture looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Downstream tools: billing API (internal), account enrichment (internal microservice), CRM lookup (third-party via API key), and a knowledge-base retrieval (ElasticSearch).
- Sample object: sending a redacted JSON in a separate attachment (datasurge-scoped-map.xlsx).
- Latency sensitivity: billing + CRM calls must be tried first and are ok to be called synchronously (we need final confirmation in the structured response). KB retrieval can be parallelized and merged.
- Security: for the PoC we prefer using API keys for internal services; for production we will likely require mutual TLS / OAuth (depending on deployment).

Two questions for Redwood team:
1) Can you sketch how you would encode function success/failure in the model response so our backend can deterministically route (we want a strict enum rather than free text).
2) For the embedding -> rerank step, we need p95 < 120ms added latency. Is that realistic if we do an index lookup + a small transformer-based reranker?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: function surface + failover options (post-demo recap)

Hannah / Ben — quick technical notes to include in our EOD plan back to DataSurge. Keeping it concise so we can operationalize in the PoC.

1) Function surface (recommendation)\- Minimal set of functions (define as strongly-typed JSON outputs):
  - billing_charge({account_id, invoice_id}) -> {status: "success"|"failed"|"retry", charge_id?: string, error_code?: string}
  - crm_lookup({email|user_id}) -> {status: "found"|"not_found", record_id?: string, score: number}
  - kb_retrieve({query, top_k}) -> {results: [{id, snippet, score}], truncated: boolean}
  - compose_response({context, actions_taken}) -> {response_type: "structured"|"free_text", payload: {...}}

Rationale: explicit statuses (enum) let downstream code avoid NLU on success/failure. Keep the payload small and JSON-schema validated server-side.

2) Parallel vs serial: hybrid approach\- Primary path (billing + crm) = serial synchronous calls (because they change state / confirm billing).\- Secondary augmentation (kb_retrieve, knowledge signals) = parallel calls invoked as background tools; merge results into a final compose_response step.

3) Error handling / failover policy\- Each tool call returns status with retries (exponential backoff up to 2 attempts).\- Idempotency keys for billing calls passed from model output to backend to avoid duplicate charges.\- If primary tool fails with permanent error -> model should emit fallback action: {action: "escalate", reason: "billing_down"} so UI shows clear next step.

4) Reranker + latency notes\- Embedding index lookup (approx 10-15ms for ~10k shard local) + lightweight cross-encoder reranker (distil-bert style small model) can hit p95 ~80-110ms if run on dedicated CPU-optimized nodes or small GPU with batching.\- Suggest: do approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW) for recall, pass top-10 to a 60-150M parameter reranker quantized to int8. Cache reranker outputs per-account for repeated queries (TTL 10m).

5) SDK + auth patterns\- PoC: recommend Redwood Python SDK for quick integration (examples for node also available). Use short-lived API keys for hosted; for private deployment support OAuth or mTLS.
- Token rotation: rotate keys every 24h for PoC; integrate with your KMS in production.

6) Structured output enforcement\- We will provide a JSON Schema for each function. The model will be prompted with the schema and a strict parse step; on validation failure we return a special wrapper: {parsing_error: true, raw_content: "..."} and trigger a single-model re-run with a higher temperature guardrail off.

I can draft the JSON Schema snippets; Hannah, want me to include a small pseudocode snippet showing the invocation + retry semantics?

Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
